embeds.title: Previously reported papers (still in the 30-day window)

fields.name: SUPRA-TEX: 3D Generation with Super-Aligned Texture
fields.value: Huawei Inc.; **FLAG: borderline** (Huawei). Note: screening had flagged "Tencent Hunyuan3D Team" as a possible co-author affiliation; Tencent Hunyuan3D only appears as a cited baseline/related-work comparison (Hunyuan3D 2.1), not as an author affiliation. The real affiliation on this paper is Huawei Inc. — SUPRA-Tex is a single-image 3D texturing method that estimates relightable materials (albedo, metallic-roughness) for the visible surface of a given mesh, aligns them precisely to that surface, and completes unobserved regions.

fields.name: Motion- and Gravity-Aware Feedforward 3D Reconstruction
fields.value: Huawei Noah's Ark Lab, Markham, Canada; **FLAG: borderline** (Huawei). — The paper targets feed-forward multi-view 3D reconstruction transformers (e.g., VGGT, π³), which the authors say rely mainly on appearance-based attention and struggle in dynamic scenes with weak geometric cues.

fields.name: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
fields.value: Tencent — GeoState proposes a view-decoupled scene-state representation for predictive 3D world modeling, built to avoid entangling scene dynamics with camera-motion-induced changes in geometry-foundation-model features.

fields.name: GRASE: Geometry-native Real-to-sim Agentic Scene Modeling from Video
fields.value: Adobe Systems — GRASE is an agentic framework that turns a captured multi-view video of a real indoor space into an editable, simulation-ready 3D scene, treating the original video as a persistent reference it checks against throughout.

fields.name: Compression of Uniformly Distributed Unit Quaternions
fields.value: AMD, Germany; **FLAG: borderline** (AMD). — The paper compares parameterizations for compressing uniformly distributed unit quaternions, a problem relevant to reducing memory and bandwidth for rotations in computer graphics.

fields.name: Anchor3DGS: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting with Compact Anchor-Based Representation
fields.value: Ant Group, Inclusion AI; Zhen-Hui Dong and Yong-Jin Liu are Tsinghua University only). **FLAG: borderline** (Ant Group; these are distinct, separately-operating companies. Screening had expected an Alibaba co-author; the real, verified affiliation is Ant Group / Inclusion AI, which does not appear in the default qualified-company list but is included here per the skill's "comparable top-tier lab, flag if unsure" rule given Ant Group's scale and its Inclusion AI research org). — Anchor3DGS is a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting method that does not require known camera poses and replaces the common one-Gaussian-per-pixel design with a compact, fixed budget of 3D anchors.

fields.name: WorldCast: Exploring Intelligent Visual Generation in World State Prediction
fields.value: Meituan; one author's footnote says work was "done during internship at Meituan"). FLAG: borderline; Meituan is kept as a large Chinese tech company with its own foundation-model line (LongCat), comparable in standing to other borderline-flagged firms, for the user to judge. — WorldCast is a 320-case, 8-category benchmark for multi-step "world state prediction" — testing whether visual generative models can produce the correct sequence of future visual states given a scenario, beyond basic text-to-image/video generation.

fields.name: What Matters for World Modeling in Vision-Language-Action Models?
fields.value: Alibaba Group — This is a controlled empirical study of how to integrate world models into Vision-Language-Action (VLA) robot policies so they predict future dynamics instead of only mapping observations to actions.

fields.name: StateCraft: Augmenting Video World Models with Abstract-State Reasoning
fields.value: Microsoft; the HTML page does not print an explicit per-author marker mapping, but Microsoft appears in the affiliation block for this author list — StateCraft decouples a persistent, updatable "abstract state" from the visual state in a video world model, so that actions can change parts of the world that are not currently visible on screen.

fields.name: OneLA: Learning Many Worlds from Latent Actions
fields.value: Alibaba Group; Junfeng Ni — OneLA learns continuous latent actions from unlabeled videos spanning games, navigation, driving, and robotics, using a shared orthonormal motion dictionary and a single predictive objective rather than task-specific designs or cross-domain alignment losses.

fields.name: Holi-Spatial 360: Generative Reconstruction from Sparse Panoramas for Spatial Rendering and Intelligence
fields.value: Tencent — Holi-Spatial 360 turns sparse real-estate panoramas of multi-room homes into annotated, photorealistic 3D environments, addressing the shortage of large-scale, semantically labeled indoor 3D data that typically requires costly LiDAR capture.

fields.name: ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis
fields.value: Meta; Ge Ya Luo's work was done at Meta. Pal is Mila/Polytechnique Montréal. — ESC targets single-image novel view synthesis under large camera changes, where 2D diffusion models can produce plausible but geometrically invalid views that standard 2D or pose metrics fail to catch.

fields.name: DeSpatial: The devil of Agentic Spatial Reasoning Lies in 3D Itself
fields.value: Tencent; exact per-author mapping not resolvable from the page). Other authors: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, Beihang University. — DeSpatial splits agentic spatial reasoning into a shared 3D perception stage — building one unified, metric, gravity-aligned scene with consistent object identities — and a separate reasoning stage that operates on that scene.
